rationale: Compose on the installed whole-bundle replacement of group eca3643289778aea5af3 by explicitly replacing bundle trial-9c6f5280d7-param-ad514673 (accepted at 3.6742565 ms vs parent 4.210417, quality pass at max_abs_error 9.5e-6 with exact top1) and re-owning its entire behavior at module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa: eval BatchNorm2d folded into bias-free conv weights at build time, fused residual add+bias+ReLU and conv bias+ReLU Triton pointwise kernels, identical aten conv2d/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear ops under the frozen FP32/no-TF32/cudnn.benchmark=False policy, the lazy side-stream warmup -> CUDA-graph capture -> verified replay flow with input-signature (shape/stride/dtype/device/data_ptr) guards, the eager fused path, and parent fallback for unsupported signatures. previous-feedback.txt contains no failure to repair: the previous trial was accepted, and its nsys/execution_timeline evidence (60 kernels, all in graph id 2, active union 3617.53us, 2.62us gaps) plus call-resources per-kernel attribution is what motivates this increment. The one measured remaining slack is the memory-bound stem epilogue: the candidate _bias_relu kernel writes the 32x64x112x112 stem activation (210.0us, grid 2048x13) and aten max_pool_forward_nchw then re-reads that activation and writes the 32x64x56x56 pooled tensor (183.6us at ~1.26TB/s achieved, the least efficient kernel in the window) - about 642MB of HBM traffic for ~230MB of useful payload. Correction to the selection note: the installed stem pooler in transformers 5.16.1 is nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1) (ResNetEmbeddings.__init__), not a 2x2/stride-2/pad-0 pool; the fused Triton kernel therefore implements exactly that 3x3/stride-2/pad-1 geometry with masked border loads (padded lanes read -inf, the max identity), guarded to accept only this geometry plus dilation 1 and ceil_mode False. Per-channel bias and ReLU commute with a spatial max for finite floats (IEEE addition and ReLU are monotonic, so max_i relu(x_i + b) == relu(max_i x_i + b) bitwise, same element selected, same per-element sums), so one fused kernel now reads the raw conv output once, applies bias+ReLU while pooling, and writes only the 25.7MB pooled tensor, deleting roughly 411MB of measured round trips (~0.15-0.28ms at the observed 1.26-2.1TB/s). CPU validation with the worker python: the kernel's window/index emulation is bitwise equal to relu(x+b) then max_pool2d(3,2,1) for 112x112 and odd/edge sizes, the plan build on the frozen assets selects the fused stem step, and the full eager pipeline matches the parent module forward to 4.1e-6 (FP32 reassociation only, same as the accepted bundle). Conv compute (~2991.6us at ~20 TFLOP/s effective FP32), workload, batch=32, precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks are untouched; measured AB/BA timing, not this estimate, decides acceptance. Route labels (cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused_stem_pool, captured, capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed, parent_fallback_unsupported_signature, setup_failure:*) remain diagnostic self-reports; the graph is captured during a real invocation on the live input storage, so replay re-executes the actual accepted work on current inputs each invocation.

setup_work.parameter_transform: At build time (torch.inference_mode(False), torch.no_grad(), so tensors stay usable in any later context; unchanged from the accepted bundle): fold the 20 eval BatchNorm2d affines (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta-mean*scale) into contiguous FP32 conv-weight copies (~44.7MB, convs stay bias-free so cudnn heuristics see identical shapes), per-channel biases with the shortcut bias pre-added per basic layer, and clone the detached classifier weight/bias (~2.1MB). Original parameters are untouched, so parent fallback and framework restore keep exact parent semantics. The stem conv keeps its folded weight/bias but its epilogue is now planned as one fused bias+ReLU+3x3/stride-2/pad-1 max-pool step.
setup_work.first_cuda_invocation: Triton JIT compile of the three kernels (_bias_relu, _add_bias_relu, and the new _bias_relu_pool3x3s2p1), side-stream warmup, CUDA graph capture of the fused static sequence, and a replay-vs-eager verification at atol=rtol=1e-4 before the graph is used - all on the first candidate CUDA call inside the adapter's real forward/inference_mode context, which precedes the timed repeats (warmup=2, quality checks first); later timed invocations replay.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates ~46.8MB of folded/cloned FP32 parameters that stay alive for the warm-model lifecycle (same as the accepted bundle; the fused stem kernel adds no new persistent parameters). The CUDA graph retains a private pool roughly the size of the activation high-water mark, which increases reserved/lifecycle_reserved bytes; because transient activations (now including the pooled stem output instead of the full 102.8MB relu'd stem activation plus its 25.7MB pooled copy) move into the graph pool, the per-run peak_allocated_bytes counter is expected to fall - an allocator-scope effect, not a physical-memory saving, and none of these counters measures the graph pool's reserved bytes as allocated.

quality_risks: The fused stem epilogue reassociates bias/ReLU with the spatial max; for finite floats this is bitwise identical to the accepted candidate's separate kernels (IEEE addition and ReLU are monotonic; CPU emulation of the exact kernel index math is bitwise equal to relu(x+b) then max_pool2d(3,2,1) for 112x112 and odd/edge sizes). Residual logits shift versus the eager parent remains the accepted bundle's FP32 reassociation (~1e-6..1e-5, previously measured max_abs_error 9.5e-6), within atol=rtol=1e-4; exact top1 can only flip if two classes are nearly tied in the reference.
Triton maximum drops NaN where aten propagates it; the frozen fixture and weights are finite, so no NaN is expected on this path (same caveat as the accepted bundle's pointwise kernels).

The fusion guard accepts only MaxPool2d(kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False) with contiguous CUDA input; every other geometry, non-contiguous input, or Triton failure takes the accepted bundle's separate relu(x+b) then F.max_pool2d sequence bitwise (self.broken latch, guarded during capture so a capture-time failure disables the graph instead of producing wrong output).

CUDA graph capture/replay can fail on unusual worker states; every graph step stays guarded (capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed route labels) and degrades to the general eager fused path, never to wrong output. The graph reads the live input storage, so mutated input contents are recomputed on each replay; different tensor objects with non-matching signatures take the eager path.

Graph replay does not re-execute the parent's inner Python calls; the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced and eliminated_calls lists every descendant again, with equivalent conv/pool/linear work continuing inside the replacement. If the evaluator rebuilds the input tensor per invocation (different data_ptr each call), the graph guard routes every call to the eager fused path: still correct, with the BN-fold, fused pointwise and fused stem-pool savings only.
